title: Joint Investigation with FIUs, Tax and Foreign Partners
summary: How to turn trade anomalies into cases by combining customs, financial and tax information, using domestic gateways and international cooperation between customs administrations, FIUs and tax authorities.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to turn trade anomalies into cases by combining customs, financial and tax information, using domestic gateways and international cooperation between customs administrations, FIUs and tax authorities.
Learning Objectives: Combine customs, financial and tax information lawfully
Use international customs, FIU and tax cooperation channels
Plan a joint investigation with clear roles and objectives
Syllabus: Domestic gateways and joint task forces
Exchange of trade data and customs mutual assistance
FIU and tax information exchange channels
Evidencing value transfer for prosecution and recovery
Intended Audience: Customs officers, trade intelligence analysts and post-clearance audit teams
FIU analysts and financial investigators handling trade-related intelligence
Tax investigators and prosecutors working on trade-linked fraud and laundering cases
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of customs, financial intelligence or financial crime investigation is helpful. No specialist knowledge of trade finance is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2010), Money Laundering Vulnerabilities of Free Trade Zones
FATF and Egmont Group (2020), Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments
FATF and Egmont Group (2021), Trade-Based Money Laundering: Risk Indicators
